subject: Post-call exec recap: AuroraMed — business outcomes & procurement path
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Baxter <tom.baxter@auroramed.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@auroramed.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call exec recap: AuroraMed — business outcomes & procurement path

Tom / Priya — thanks again for a productive conversation today. Quick recap for execs and next steps so we have alignment. If I've missed anything, please flag.

Key pain points we heard
- Production document ingestion and search is inconsistent: index lag and stale embeddings causing clinical staff to see outdated results.
- Current 3rd-party provider has high per-token costs and unpredictable latency at peak (reports of 1200–1500ms p95).
- Security and auditability are non-negotiable — procurement requires SOC2 evidence and data residency controls.

Business outcomes AuroraMed is targeting
- Reduce mean time-to-find (clinical info) by 40% to improve clinician throughput.
- Cut inference costs by ~30% through caching/batching and model selection.
- Achieve SOC2-equivalent evidence for procurement to approve a pilot and Team-based access controls for PHI-safe handling.

Technical notes from the call
- Target inference workload: ~300 concurrent users, avg seq len 512, peak bursts to 700 QPS for embeddings and reranking.
- Ideal pilot: 6 weeks, ingest 500k docs, run A/B against current provider on NRR and latency.

Commercial / procurement path
- AuroraMed indicated a preference for a pilot followed by a reserved capacity commit if performance and cost metrics are met.
- Procurement will require SOC2 artifacts + SLAs; they asked for an initial commercial outline and draft SOW.

Immediate next steps (owners and timeline)
1) Redwood to share: pricing outline + 6-week pilot SOW + SOC2 evidence spreadsheet — by EOD 8/2. (Owner: Marissa)  
2) AuroraMed to confirm procurement contact and desired pilot metrics (NRR, latency p95 targets) — by 8/4. (Owner: Tom / Priya)
3) Schedule technical kickoff (redwood infra + Aurora infra) the week of 8/9 — 30–45m. (Owner: Aditya)
4) Executive alignment: Laura to join if exec sponsor wants a 15m alignment call. (Owner: Laura)

Attachments: Aurora_Redwood_MA_Pricing_v1.pdf (pricing + pilot SOW), SOC2-evidence-request.xlsx (spreadsheet of standard artifacts).

Short signature
—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Date: 2027-08-02T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Exec recap + risk & escalation items — AuroraMed pilot proposal

Priya / Tom — looping in Laura (head of enterprise) and Markus (procurement) so execs have a concise summary for their internal review. Below is an "executive brief" you can forward to stakeholders.

Executive brief (one-pager)
Objective: Run a 6-week pilot to validate latency, cost, and accuracy improvements for AuroraMed's clinical search and knowledge workflows. If pilot meets agreed SLAs, move to a reserved capacity commitment for predictable performance and lower unit costs.

Expected outcomes (KPIs)
- Latency: reduce generation p95 to <450ms for typical queries.
- Cost: reduce per-inference cost by ~30% vs current provider through batching, KV caching, and model tuning.
- Accuracy/UX: preserve or improve top-3 retrieval relevance as measured by AuroraMed's test set.

Primary risks and mitigations
- Data security / compliance: procurement will need SOC2 artifacts — Redwood will provide SOC2 evidence and a completed questionnaire within 48 hours of signature. We can also enable VPC-isolated deployment if required.
- Integration complexity: prioritize a small canonical dataset for the pilot to reduce integration scope (500k docs).
- Executive buy-in: propose a 15m exec alignment call (Redwood: Laura + Marissa; AuroraMed: Priya) before pilot start.

Procurement path & timeline
- 8/2: Redwood sends pricing + SOW + SOC2 artifact spreadsheet (today).
- 8/4: AuroraMed confirms metrics and procurement contact details.
- 8/9–8/13: Technical kickoff + exec alignment.
- 8/16: Pilot starts (6 weeks).

Escalation points
- If we cannot meet latency p95 target within first 2 weeks, trigger technical deep-dive and (if needed) temporary increase in reserved capacity for pilot to meet user experience targets.
- If procurement raises additional legal/PII concerns, route to our security team (cc: laura_bennett) for rapid response.

Commercial note (high level)
- Proposed pilot credit: Redwood is prepared to provide a 25% pilot credit contingent on data access and joint benchmark execution. Aditya will follow up with a draft commercial term sheet and SOW.

Next steps (re-stated)
- Marissa: attach pricing + SOC2 spreadsheet (sent).
- Aditya: schedule tech kickoff and share onboarding checklist.
- AuroraMed: share procurement contact and confirm pilot metrics by 8/4.

Best —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
